transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I'm here because... well, I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. I mean, I'm sure it's probably nothing major, but I just can't seem to keep my head clear. 

It's actually a bit embarrassing to admit, but I'll be sitting there and I just sort of... lose track of what my clients are saying to me. And then I'll catch myself rereading the exact same chart note over and over again. I even kind of freeze up on really simple decisions that I used to handle with no problem at all. I really want to do a good job for them, so it's been bothering me. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with focusing and decision-making?

Um, I'd say... well, it's been going on for about a month now. I really didn't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know everyone at the clinic is stressed and I don't want to sound like I'm complaining. We lost some staff recently, so my schedule got shifted into late-evening coverage, and I've had to take on a lot heavier crisis paperwork. 

I'm sure it's probably just a normal adjustment period, right? I really don't want it to seem like I can't handle my job... I just, I hope it makes sense why I might be a little off my game lately? Is it okay that I'm bringing this up?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started having these difficulties with focusing and decision-making?

Um, sad? I mean... I wouldn't really use the word sad, exactly. I don't want to sound like I'm whining about things, you know? It's more just... I guess I've been feeling a little tired, maybe a bit flat? 

I just figure everyone gets a little run down sometimes, right? Especially with the extra hours and everything. I try to keep a positive attitude for my clients, I really do. I don't think I'm, like, depressed or anything like that. I just... I don't know, maybe I'm just not trying hard enough to shake it off? Does that sound like a normal reaction to the stress, do you think?
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Um, I mean, I'm sure it's just because I've been so busy with work, you know? But... I guess I haven't really been doing much of my usual stuff lately. 

I don't want it to sound like I'm completely giving up on things, but my guitar has just been sitting in the corner for a while. And, um, I keep bailing on my weekend soccer games and my shifts at the animal shelter. I feel really bad about it, I hate letting people down. I've tried to force myself to do things, like cooking a nice meal or going for a hike, but it just... it feels like I'm just going through the motions. Like there's no real point to it? 

I know I should be making more of an effort to stay active. I'm probably just being lazy, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person... is it normal to just kind of lose your spark when work gets heavy?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?

Um, anxious? I don't think so, really. I mean, maybe a tiny bit stressed with the new schedule, but definitely not on edge or anything like that. I try really hard to stay calm and grounded, especially since I need to be present for my clients. 

I really wouldn't say I'm an anxious person. I mean, everyone gets a little overwhelmed sometimes, right? But I'm definitely not walking around feeling panicked or anything. I hope I'm explaining that okay? I just don't want you to think I'm, like, falling apart at the seams over a little extra paperwork.
Do you feel like you're still able to find pleasure in the things you're doing, even if it's just going through the motions?

Um, pleasure? I... I really wish I could say yes, because I know I should be enjoying these things. I mean, I have a good life, you know? But... no, not really. 

Like I was saying about the guitar and soccer and the shelter... even when I do push myself to go for a hike or cook something nice, it's just... it's like eating cardboard, I guess? I'm doing the steps, but there's no joy in it. I just feel kind of blank. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so ungrateful. I really am trying to snap out of it and appreciate things more. Do you think that's something I can fix if I just try harder to focus on the positive?
Have you lost any weight recently?

Um, weight? I haven't been on a scale recently, so I can't give you an exact number. I'm sure it's nothing drastic, though. I mean, my pants have gotten a little loose, but that's probably just normal fluctuation, right? 

I guess I have been skipping meals a bit lately, but honestly, it's just because I get so caught up in things and forget. Most days I don't even realize I'm hungry until a friend or someone reminds me to eat. I really don't want it to seem like I'm neglecting myself on purpose or anything. I know it's important to eat right, especially when you're trying to help other people, you know? I'm definitely going to try to be better about eating regular meals. Does that sound like a good plan?
Would you say that you've lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I guess... um, it kind of goes back to what I was just saying a minute ago? About, you know, the guitar and soccer and volunteering at the shelter. I just haven't had the drive for them lately. My guitar has basically just been sitting in the corner gathering dust, and I keep bailing on my soccer team and my shifts at the shelter... which I feel awful about, really. I hate letting people down, and I know I need to be more reliable. 

But even when I do try to force myself to do things, like when I try to cook a nice meal or go hiking, it just feels like going through the motions with no real point to it. I really don't want to sound lazy or anything, I promise I'm usually a really active and involved person! I just... I guess I've lost that spark for a little bit. But I'm sure I can get it back if I just push myself a little harder and stay disciplined, right? I really want to get back to my normal self.
Would you say you've been feeling depressed, even if it's just a little bit, most of the time since you started having these difficulties?

Um, depressed? I... I don't know if I would use that word. I really don't want to sound dramatic, you know? There are people out there with much bigger problems, so I'd feel terrible complaining and calling myself depressed when I have so much to be thankful for. 

I don't really sit around feeling super sad or crying or anything like that. It's more just... that blank, empty feeling I was talking about earlier. I'm still trying my absolute best to keep a smile on and be upbeat, especially because I know how important it is to bring good energy when you're helping others. So, no, I wouldn't really say I feel depressed most of the time. Just maybe a little stuck in a rut right now? 

I hope it's okay that I don't see it as depression... I just really think I need to focus on being more positive and pushing through it, right?
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight over the past month?

Um, I know we kind of touched on this just a bit ago... I haven't really been tracking it with a scale or anything, so I can't give you a precise number. I really hope that's okay. 

Like I mentioned, my pants have definitely gotten a bit loose over the last few weeks. I guess I've just been skipping meals without really meaning to. It's not that I'm trying to lose weight or anything, I promise! It's just... most days I don't even feel hungry until someone actually reminds me that I need to eat. I know I should be taking better care of myself, and I really don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose. I'm definitely going to try and set reminders on my phone to eat more regularly, if that sounds like a good idea to you?
Do you feel like you're just going through the motions of daily life without any real emotional response, or are there times when you actually feel a sad or depressed mood?

Um, yeah, I guess it's mostly just going through the motions. Like I was saying, it's just that sort of empty, blank feeling? I really don't feel sad or... or depressed. I mean, I don't sit around crying or anything, I promise. I try really hard to keep a good attitude. 

I know I should probably be feeling more, um, engaged with things, and I feel bad that I'm not. I don't want to come across like I'm ungrateful or just complaining. It's just... I guess I'm just feeling a little flat right now? But no, not sad. I really hope that makes sense and it's okay that I'm not feeling sad... I'm really trying to focus on the positive, you know?
Do you ever feel a sad or depressed mood, even if it's just for a short time?

Um, honestly, no. I really don't think I do. I know we just talked about this, and I hope it's not frustrating that my answer is the same, but... yeah, I really don't get sad or down like that. 

Even for short times, it's just... more of that blankness, you know? I really try my best to not let myself get to a sad place. I feel like if I start feeling sorry for myself, I'm just letting people down, especially the people I work with. I really want to be someone who brings positivity, so I just... I don't really let myself feel sad. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's alright that I don't have those moments of feeling depressed. I just really want to keep pushing forward and doing my best.
Do you ever feel a low or depressed mood, even if it's just for a moment?

Um... I'm really sorry, I know we keep coming back to this, and I feel terrible if I'm not giving you the answer you need for your notes. But... honestly, no. Not even for a moment. 

I really don't get that low or depressed feeling. Like I was saying, I try really hard to keep a good mindset. I know how important it is to stay steady, especially for my work—I feel like I need to be strong and positive for the people I'm helping, you know? I can't really afford to let myself get down. 

I promise I'd tell you if I was feeling depressed. I'm just dealing with that sort of blankness we talked about. Is it... is it okay if we just put down that I don't really get sad? I really hope I'm not messing up your evaluation or making your job harder by repeating myself.
Can you think of any time recently when you felt a little down or depressed, even if it was just for a brief moment?

Um... no, I really can't. I'm so sorry, I know you're just doing your job and trying to be thorough, and I feel awful that I keep giving you the exact same answer. I really hope you don't think I'm being difficult or hiding something. 

I just... I really don't feel down or depressed. Even briefly. I just try to keep a smile on and focus on helping others, you know? Being a therapist, I have to be the strong one for my clients. They rely on me. If I let myself get down, I wouldn't be doing them any good, and I really don't want to let anyone down. 

So, yeah, it's just that flat feeling. Nothing sad. Is that... is that an okay answer? I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for this.
Do you think you might be feeling depressed without realizing it?

Um... I mean, I guess it's possible? I'm sorry, I don't want to sound like I'm arguing with you or anything. You're the expert, so if you think that's what's happening, I definitely wouldn't say you're wrong. 

It's just... I really don't *feel* depressed. I know I've said that a lot, and I'm really sorry to keep repeating it. I just try so hard to be upbeat and present for my clients, and I feel like if I were actually depressed, I wouldn't be able to do my job right, you know? And I really, really don't want to be failing them. 

But... if you think this blankness I'm feeling is actually depression hiding itself... is that a thing? I really want to understand what you're seeing. I hope I'm not being too confusing or making this difficult for you to figure out. Do you think I'm depressed without knowing it?
Can you think of any situation or event in the past month that made you feel even slightly tearful or sad?

Um... I'm really trying to rack my brain here, because I want to give you a helpful answer... but, honestly, no. I can't think of anything. I haven't felt tearful or sad about anything this past month. 

I'm really sorry, I know I keep giving you the exact same kind of response, and I feel terrible if it seems like I'm not cooperating or not thinking hard enough about your questions. I just... even if something stressful happens, I don't really cry or get sad about it. I just sort of brush it off and keep going. 

Is it... is it bad if I don't have an example for you? I really hope I'm not messing up your assessment by not having the right kind of answers.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find pleasure in only slightly or not at all?

Um... yeah, I guess there are a few things. I'm really sorry to admit this, because I know I should be keeping up with my hobbies, and I feel bad that I've been letting them slide. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or giving up on things.

It's just... my guitar has been sitting in the corner for a while now. And I keep bailing on my soccer games and my volunteer shifts at the animal shelter. I know that's terrible of me, especially letting down the shelter and my team. I really hate being unreliable. 

Even when I force myself to try and do things I used to love, like cooking a nice meal or going for a hike... it just feels like I'm going through the motions. Like there's no point to it, and I don't get that spark of enjoyment I used to. 

Is that... does that make sense? I'm sorry, I really hope I'm not sounding too negative. I'm trying my best to stay active, I promise. Is it normal to just lose the fun in things like that?
Do you feel like there's anything that's been bothering you or weighing on your mind lately?

Um... honestly? Not really. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm holding out on you or trying to be difficult, because I really do want to help you figure this out. But... no, nothing is really bothering me. 

My life is actually pretty okay, and I feel kind of guilty even taking up your time when I don't have any real problems weighing on my mind. I know there are people out there dealing with so much worse, so I try not to complain. I just... I don't really have a good reason or a specific stressor to point to for why I've been feeling so blank. 

I really hope that's an okay answer and I'm not making your job harder. Is it... is it normal to feel so out of it when nothing is actually wrong?
Do you feel like you've been having a depressed mood for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

Um... I wouldn't say depressed, exactly. I really hope that's the right word to use... I don't want to sound dramatic or like I'm exaggerating things. 

It's more just... like I said, kind of blank? Or flat. I guess it has been most of the day for the last couple of weeks, but I wouldn't call it sad or depressed. I'm still getting up and going to work and everything, so I'm really trying to keep it together. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all day. 

I'm sorry if I'm not giving you a clear "yes" or "no." I just want to make sure I'm being accurate so I don't give you the wrong impression. Does that make sense? Is it okay if I just call it feeling flat instead of depressed?
Do you feel like you've been having a low mood most of the time since your symptoms started?

Um... well, like I was saying, I wouldn't really call it a low mood, exactly. I hope that's okay to say. I just don't want to make it sound worse than it is, you know? 

I mean, I guess it's been pretty consistent since all this started, but it's really more of that... that empty feeling. Not sad or down, just kind of... there. I'm really trying my best not to let it get to me, and I don't want to come across like I'm complaining about being sad all the time when I'm not. 

Is it alright if I describe it like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I'm actually being helpful to you.
